items.t: "Langley" on this page is two municipalities: the City of Langley, under Zoning Bylaw 1996, No. 2100, and the Township of Langley, under Zoning Bylaw 1987, No. 2500, and a penthouse unit's rules depend on which one the building sits in.
City of Langley apartment growth in the documents read is on Eastleigh Crescent, designated Transit-Oriented Residential and Low Rise Residential in the City's Official Community Plan (OCP).
The City of Langley apartment form in the bylaws read is low-rise: a 6-storey, 136-unit building at 20619 and 20629 Eastleigh Crescent, rezoned to Comprehensive Development Zone CD92.
A second Eastleigh building, 20719 to 20731 Eastleigh Crescent, is 5 storeys and 132 units, applicant Whitetail Homes Ltd., rezoned to CD95.

blocks.text: Langley Penthouses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: In the Township, lands in the Willowbrook Transit-Oriented Area are exempt from required off-street parking for residential uses, except parking for persons with disabilities, under the amendment to Zoning Bylaw 1987, No. 2500.

In the City, all lands designated Transit-Oriented Residential are subject to a development permit for building form and character, so top-floor form is set site by site in a CD zone, not by a general penthouse rule.
The CD92 Eastleigh approval required 203 parking spaces and provided 169, including visitor spaces, a variance pattern a penthouse buyer should expect in City CD zones.

blocks.text: Langley Penthouses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The CD95 Eastleigh site was assembled from Strata Lots 1 and 2 of Strata Plan NW2601, a reminder that City apartment sites are often strata conversions.
Both Eastleigh approvals varied visitor parking down to 20 spaces, so guest parking in newer City buildings is set by variance, not by the base zone.

blocks.text: Langley Penthouses: development and new projects

items.t: Apartment building, 20619 and 20629 Eastleigh Crescent, City of Langley: 6 storeys, 136 units, CD92. STATUS: rezoning and development permit application DP 08-23 in the bylaw read 2026-11-03; no penthouse product stated.

Apartment building, 20719 to 20731 Eastleigh Crescent, applicant Whitetail Homes Ltd.: 5 storeys, 132 units, CD95. STATUS: rezoning and development permit application DP 13-23 in the bylaw read 2026-11-03; no penthouse product stated.
The Eastleigh Crescent buildings sit in areas the City designates Transit-Oriented Residential and Low Rise Residential, which is the planning basis for their height and reduced parking.

blocks.text: Langley Penthouses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Read the building's own CD zone before assuming a roof deck or top-floor addition is permitted: CD92 and CD95 each carry site-specific height, coverage and parking schedules.
Confirm the municipality first: applying Township rules to a City building, or the reverse, is the main error risk on this page, because the bylaws share zone names but not numbers.

blocks.text: What is not confirmed about Langley Penthouses

items.t: Sourced material above is about the two municipalities' apartment rules, not about any named penthouse.
Named buildings with penthouse or top-floor product: none confirmed.

faq.q: What should I check before buying a penthouse in Langley?
faq.a: Read the Form B, the bylaws, the strata minutes and the depreciation report, and ask about roof, balcony and window repairs, since top-floor units are the ones exposed to them.

faq.q: What makes a penthouse different from other condos in Langley?
faq.a: A penthouse is a top-floor unit, usually with more floor area, higher ceilings and larger outdoor space than the units below. Strata fees and property taxes usually follow the size, so compare the full monthly cost, not just the price.
